newsitem.title: UK: UK vows freedom of information paper despite delay.
newsitem.headline: UK vows freedom of information paper despite delay.

text.p: The new Labour government on Friday dismissed reports that it was dragging its feet over its election manifesto promise to introduce freedom of information legislation.

"We have been criticised in some quarters for delay on this front. I can assure you that the government is determined to put a Freedom of Information Act on the statute book," Scottish Secretary Donald Dewar said.
"We intend to engage in full and open consultation prior to legislation," Dewar told a conference on constitutional reform.

He said a consultative white paper that will precede the bill, designed to open up the workings of government to the public, would be published shortly, but officials admitted it would not be ready before parliament's long summer recess.
They said the new government's heavy workload and the difficulty of drawing up proposals in a complicated area meant ministers needed more time to get the paper right.
Officials played down a BBC report that opposition by senior civil servants was delaying the white paper. "It is ministers taking time to ensure we get it right," one said.
